title: Token-path Explorer — PRD and Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This document defines the Product Requirements Document (PRD) and rollout playbook for the Token-path Explorer: an offline consumption scenario builder and simulator that predicts per-tenant token economics across model variants, runtime configurations (batching, caching, quantization), and routing policies. The tool will be used by product, solutions engineering, and sales to: estimate cost, validate SLO trade-offs, and generate migration/runbook recommendations for customers moving between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Context and motivation
----------------------
- Customers and internal teams repeatedly ask for reproducible cost/latency forecasts for particular workloads before migrating to Dedicated or enabling quantized variants.
- Existing cost calculators are surface-level (per-token multipliers). They do not model sequence shape, KV cache locality, batch formation dynamics, or fallback routing economics.
- Token-path Explorer (TPE) aims to close this gap with an offline simulator that takes sampled request traces, an SLO profile, and model/runtime knobs and produces: realistic cost/latency distributions, sensitivity analyses, and an actionable migration playbook.

Goals (outcomes)
----------------
1) Provide 90% accurate cost and p95 latency forecasts (compared to controlled bench runs) for typical multi-tenant conversational workloads.
2) Surface the top-3 cost drivers per tenant and recommend configuration deltas (batch limit, prefix cache TTL, quantization level, routing tier).
3) Generate an automated migration playbook (checklist + run commands) for Hosted -> Dedicated or Dedicated -> Private transitions.
4) Produce exportable artifacts: CSV cost-breakdowns, PDF runbook, and a reproducible job definition for offline reruns.

Non-goals
---------
- This is not a real-time estimator embedded in the Console. TPE is offline/batch only in v1.
- TPE will not perform live traffic injection or runtime changes automatically. All runbook changes require operator approval.

User personas and primary use cases
----------------------------------
- Solutions Engineer: run a tenant trace, produce a migration cost/latency brief for sales.
- Product Manager: perform sensitivity experiments for packaging and SLA adjustments.
- ML Engineer / Platform: validate that a quantized variant meets p99 latency and quality budgets before rollout.

High-level solution overview
----------------------------
- Inputs:
  - Request trace (JSONL) with timestamps, routing decisions, sequence lengths, token counts, and optional dialogue/session IDs.
  - Model variants catalog (JSON) with per-variant perf profiles: tokens/sec baseline, memory footprint, quantized token-multiplier, and fallback compatibility list.
  - Runtime configuration: batch size distribution, batch formation window (ms), prefix/KV cache hit rate model, coldstart probabilities, and regional routing map.
  - SLO / target: p50/p95 latency thresholds, cost budget per million tokens, and max acceptable quality delta (ROUGE/BLEU/LLM-score).
- Core engine:
  - Event-driven simulator that processes the trace, simulates batching behavior, computes KV cache hits (session-aware), applies quantization multipliers and kernel-level throughput constraints, and models fallback routing when capacity is saturated.
  - Output generator: latency and cost distributions, per-token cost decomposition (compute, memory, network), and sensitivity sweeps.
- Outputs:
  - Summary dashboard (HTML/PDF) with charts: latency CDFs, cost waterfall, top cost contributors, and recommended config diffs.
  - Runbook (Markdown/PDF): step-by-step migration/playbook for the recommended configuration changes and monitoring hooks.
  - Machine-readable job spec for reproducibility (YAML).

Requirements (MUST have)
------------------------
1) Trace ingestion: accept gzipped JSONL traces up to 10GB. Trace schema must include: request_id, tenant_id, timestamp_ms, seq_len_prompt, seq_len_completion_est, session_id (optional), model_hint (optional).
2) Model perf catalog: JSON schema with fields: model_name, hardware_profile (e.g., A100-80GB), base_tokens_per_sec, quantization_levels (map: q4->multiplier), max_sequence_supported.
3) Batching model: configurable batch_window_ms and max_batch_size. Simulator must implement first-come-first-batch and sliding-window batching heuristics.
4) KV cache model: implement session-aware caching with configurable TTL, hit probability curve by sequence prefix overlap, and configurable KV hit latency delta.
5) Fallback/routing simulation: model capacity per-region and implement backpressure policies (reject, queue, fallback-to-lower-fidelity-variant) with configurable probabilities for each failover path.
6) Output accuracy: when running on synthetic traces with known baselines, the cost prediction must be within ±10% of measured compute cost and p95 latency within ±15% for at least 90% of test cases.
7) Export formats: CSV (per-tenant per-run), PDF summary, and YAML job spec.
8) Access control: only members of product, solutions-eng, and platform infra groups can create/run jobs; results must be scannable by sales via a shared read-only link.

Acceptance criteria
-------------------
- Demo run: team can run a tenant trace and produce a PDF brief with cost and p95 latency plots within 20 minutes on a small runner (8 vCPU, 32GB RAM).
- Automated test suite: unit tests for batching semantics and cache model; integration tests asserting predictions against a set of curated traces.
- Security review: passes internal security checklist for handling customer traces (PII stripping, encryption-at-rest during runs).

Detailed design notes
---------------------
1) Batching engine pseudocode:
   - On arrival of request r at t: put in pending queue for tenant T. Start batch window if not already started. At batch_window_ms expiry or when pending_count >= max_batch_size assemble batch.
   - For each assembled batch: compute effective tokens_per_sec as min(sum(base_throughputs), kernel_throughput_limit) * batching_efficiency_factor(seq_shape).
2) KV cache modeling:
   - Use session_id to group requests. Compute prefix_overlap = longest_common_prefix(past_prompts, current_prompt) / current_prompt_tokens. Map prefix_overlap to hit_rate via configurable piecewise-linear function.
3) Quantization impact:
   - For quantized level q: effective_tokens_cost = base_compute_cost * quantization_levels[q]. Also set memory footprint and potential quality delta pulled from eval lab.
4) Fallback policy templates:
   - Template A (cost-first): when capacity exceeded, route to quantized variant in same region; if unavailable route to remote region; if still unavailable return token-limited partial response.
   - Template B (latency-first): prefer same-region model; accept higher cost by spinning up burst capacity from reserved pool.

API and CLI examples
--------------------
- Job YAML (minimal)
  ```yaml
  job_name: acme-payments-q3-migration
  trace_file: s3://trace-buckets/acme/2026-09/tenant-123.jsonl.gz
  model_catalog: s3://catalogs/release-2026-09/models.json
  runtime_config:
    batch_window_ms: 12
    max_batch_size: 64
    kv_cache_ttl_seconds: 3600
    fallback_policy: cost-first
  slo:
    p95_latency_ms: 700
    cost_budget_per_million_tokens_usd: 9.50
  outputs:
    - pdf_summary: s3://tpe-results/acme-2026-09/brief.pdf
    - csv_breakdown: s3://tpe-results/acme-2026-09/breakdown.csv
  ```
- CLI (runner)
  $ tpe run --job job.yaml --runner-host runner-01 --parallelism 4 --encrypt-output

Operational runbook (playbook)
------------------------------
1) Prep: obtain sanitized trace from customer and ensure PII stripping. Upload to customer-specific S3 with kms encryption.
2) Execute: create job YAML, set batch_window_ms baseline to 12ms and max_batch_size to 64. Run on runner pool tagged "tpe-runner-small".
3) Validate: confirm produced PDF includes waterfall and top-3 recommendations.
4) Sanity checks: inspect p95 latency heatmap and check that recommended quant-level quality delta <= customer threshold.
5) Deliver: attach brief to customer ticket and notify SE via Slack #se-results.

Rollout plan and milestones
--------------------------
- v0.1 (6 weeks): CLI runner + basic batching + model catalog ingestion + PDF export. Internal-only.
- v0.2 (12 weeks): KV cache model, fallback simulation, sensitivity sweeps, and runbook generation. SE alpha.
- v1.0 (20 weeks): Access controls, integrated job UI in Console (read-only links), exportable job specs, and security review. GA to Solutions Eng and Sales.

SLOs / metrics for TPE service
-----------------------------
- Job success rate: >= 98% for valid job specs.
- Job runtime: 95% of small jobs complete under 20 minutes.
- Prediction fidelity: see requirement 6 above.

Security and compliance notes
-----------------------------
- All traces must be processed using a private runner in a customer-isolated VPC if the customer marks them restricted.
- PII detection step required before ingestion; any detected PII must be redacted using the standard PII-redaction library.
- Outputs stored in S3 must be encrypted with customer KMS keys when available.

Monitoring and observability
---------------------------
- Expose metrics: jobs.started, jobs.completed, jobs.failed, job.duration_seconds (histogram), prediction.delta_cost_pct (histogram).
- Dashboard: create a Grafana dashboard under team "platform" with per-run cards and aggregated weekly fidelity drift.

Ownership and stakeholders
-------------------------
- Product (owner): Asha Patel
- Solutions Engineering: Diego Morales (primary SE contact)
- Platform/Infra: Evan Brooks (runner infra), Priya Nandakumar (security review)
- Sales enablement: Samantha Li

Open questions and risks
------------------------
1) How to validate simulated quality delta for quantized models without running expensive lab evals? (Mitigation: use historical model eval curves and conservative safety margins.)
2) Risk of PII leakage from customer traces. (Mitigation: mandatory PII detector + encrypted ephemeral runners.)
3) Potential mismatch between offline simulation and live autoscaling behavior. (Mitigation: include calibration step comparing a small controlled live test against predictions.)

Appendices
---------
A) Trace schema (example JSONL line):
  {"request_id":"r-01","tenant_id":"t-123","timestamp_ms":1696000123456,"seq_len_prompt":120,"seq_len_completion_est":256,"session_id":"s-abc","model_hint":"gptx-small"}

B) Quick checklist for SEs before delivering a brief:
  1. Confirm PII scrubbed and KMS keys in place.
  2. Run baseline job with current production config.
  3. Run 3 sensitivity sweeps: batch_window (6/12/24ms), quant-levels (fp16/q4/q8), cache TTL (300/3600/86400s).
  4. Validate runbook tests and attach artifacts.

C) Minimal integration test cases:
  - small conversational trace with strong session locality -> expect high KV hit rate and reduced cost.
  - high fanout short prompts -> batching inefficiency and increased p95.
  - mixed long-tail prompts that trigger fallback -> verify fallback routing cost delta.

Release notes (draft)
---------------------
- v0.1 (internal) 2026-11-15: CLI runner, basic batching semantics, model catalog ingestion, PDF and CSV exports.
